The plasma-assisted cases exhibit modest reductions in peak cylinder pressure and HRR, along with improved combustion consistency, confirming more complete oxidation and smoother pressure development. ............................................................................................ 17 Southwest Research Institute® U.S. DOE Award Number DE-FE0032301 Public Version - v - DE-FE0032301 Final Report SECTION 1 — Executive Summary 1.1 Project Purpose and Motivation Methane slip from natural-gas-fueled compressor engines is a significant source of methane leaks in midstream operations. Retrofitting existing engines to reduce unburned methane offers a near- term path for industry compliance should regulations change. The objective of this project was to develop and demonstrate a retrofit-capable plasma fuel reformer that reduces methane slip without altering engine architecture or requiring an external hydrogen supply. 1.2 Technical Approach The system employs pulsed plasma to partially reform methane into hydrogen and acetylene, species known to increase combustion flame speed and oxidation efficiency. A dual-zone reformer and compact 4 kW power-electronics module were designed, fabricated, and validated through four phases: 1. Concept Design and Modeling – computational fluid-dynamics (CFD) simulation and power system specification. 2. Bench-Scale Testing – laboratory verification of plasma formation, hydrogen yield, and energy efficiency. 3. High-Flow Testing – operation at Southwest Research Institute’s (SwRI’s) MRF to define stable plasma conditions up to 300 standard liters per minute (SLPM) and 20 psig.
